title: CareerLoop Mains Exam — Set 01
patternNote: CareerLoop mains paper covering General Intelligence & Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, English Language and General Awareness. 30 original questions written for CareerLoop / 40 minutes / +2 per correct / −0.5 per wrong.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Find the next number in the series: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 7, 9, 11 — consecutive odd numbers. The next difference is 13, so 35 + 13 = 48.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: ACE : GIK :: MOQ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter of the first group is moved six places forward: A→G, C→I, E→K. Applying the same shift to MOQ gives S, U, W.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: In a certain code TRAIN is written as USBJO. How is PLANE written in that code?
questions.explanation: Every letter is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet (T→U, R→S, A→B, I→J, N→O). So P→Q, L→M, A→B, N→O, E→F, giving QMBOF.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: A man walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Walking 5 km north then 5 km south cancels the north-south movement. He is left 3 km to the east of the start, so the distance is 3 km.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl in the photograph related to Ravi?
questions.explanation: Ravi's grandfather's only son is Ravi's father. The daughter of Ravi's father is Ravi's sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are red. Conclusions: I. Some pens are red. II. Some books are pens. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: Conclusion II is the direct converse of 'All pens are books' and always holds. The red books need not include any pen, so conclusion I does not follow.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 200
questions.explanation: 121 = 11², 144 = 12² and 169 = 13² are perfect squares. 200 is not a perfect square.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Complete the series: AZ, BY, CX, ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) while the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W). The next pair is DW.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: What is 15% of 480?

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5 and their sum is 64. What is the larger number?
questions.explanation: The total of the ratio parts is 8, so one part is 64 ÷ 8 = 8. The larger number is 5 × 8 = 40.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: The average of five numbers is 28. If one number, 40, is removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: The total is 5 × 28 = 140. Removing 40 leaves 100, and 100 ÷ 4 = 25.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 of the job per day. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: A train 120 m long is running at 54 km/h. How long does it take to pass a pole?
questions.explanation: 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Time = distance ÷ speed = 120 ÷ 15 = 8 seconds.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: An article costing ₹400 is sold for ₹460. What is the profit percentage?

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: Find the simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.stem: What is 25% of 320 plus 40% of 150?
questions.explanation: 25% of 320 = 80 and 40% of 150 = 60. Their sum is 140.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'abundant'.
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities, so 'plentiful' is the synonym. The other three words mean the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'frugal'.
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means sparing with money. Its opposite is 'extravagant'. 'Thrifty' and 'economical' are synonyms, not antonyms.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: What does the idiom 'to let the cat out of the bag' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to disclose something that was meant to be kept secret.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Identify the grammatically incorrect part: (A) Each of the students (B) have submitted (C) the assignment (D) No error
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb must be singular: 'Each of the students has submitted the assignment.'

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Fill in the blank: She has been living here ______ 2015.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time (2015). 'For' is used with a duration, such as 'for ten years'.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: One word for 'a person who cannot read or write' is:
questions.explanation: 'Illiterate' describes someone unable to read or write. 'Illegible' describes handwriting that cannot be read.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodation', with double c and double m.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra is the capital of Australia. Sydney and Melbourne are larger cities but not the capital.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Article 14 guarantees equality before the law.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland in the human body. It produces bile and performs many metabolic functions.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who wrote 'The Discovery of India'?
questions.explanation: 'The Discovery of India' was written by Jawaharlal Nehru while he was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is the longest river flowing within India. The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol of sodium?
questions.explanation: The chemical symbol of sodium is Na, from its Latin name 'natrium'. 'S' is the symbol for sulphur.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
questions.explanation: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. It was established in 1995.
